conventions.convention: Sign/orientation convention for Hamiltonian actions: the fundamental field is ξ_M(p) = d/dt|_0 exp_G(−tξ)·p and the component moment equations are dμ^ξ = −ι_{ξ_M}ω; with this convention the cotangent-lift moment map is ⟨μ(q,p),ξ⟩ = −p(ξ_Q(q)).

Two distinct notions are kept apart: an infinitesimal moment map satisfies only the component equations dμ^ξ = −ι_{ξ_M}ω, while an equivariant moment map additionally satisfies μ(g·p) = g·μ(p) for the coadjoint action; a Hamiltonian action is a symplectic action admitting an equivariant moment map.

Reduced-dimension convention: at a regular value α with free proper G_α-action, dim M_α = dim M − dim G − dim G_α, specialising to dim M − 2 dim G only at α = 0; the value α enters only through dim G_α.
KKS normalization: ω_β(ξ_O(β), η_O(β)) = β([ξ,η]), and the coadjoint orbit carries the injectively immersed homogeneous-space structure transported from G/G_α (not an embedded structure).

Cartan subalgebras are defined abstractly (nilpotent and self-normalising, dim equals the rank via the minimal eigenspace dimension); the identification with maximal toral subalgebras is a theorem for complex semisimple algebras, not part of the definition, and for real algebras neither compact nor split Cartan subalgebras need be conjugate.

Dominance and integrality of a weight λ are defined relative to a chosen positive system: ⟨λ,α_i^∨⟩ ∈ ℤ_{≥0} for the simple coroots, so the notion is not choice-free (the opposite positive system reverses it).
The Weyl vector is ρ = ½ Σ_{α>0} α, asserted only to lie in ½Q (the factor ½ is the real scalar ½; no integrality of ρ is claimed), and it depends on the chosen positive system.

Compact-group circle convention: S^1 = R/Z, with character values transported to the multiplicative unit circle by [r] ↦ e^{2πir}; root differentials are imaginary on t and real on it, and characters are identified with the integral weight lattice of T.

Cartan involution convention: θ is an involutive automorphism with B_θ(X,Y) = −B(X,θY) positive definite; k_0 is the (+1)-eigenspace (B negative definite) and p_0 the (−1)-eigenspace (B positive definite), and these signs are used throughout.

Real-form convention: a real form g_0 satisfies g = g_0 ⊕ i g_0 with g_0 ∩ i g_0 = 0, and corresponds to the conjugate-linear involution σ(X+iY) = X − iY with fixed locus g_0; conjugacy of forms means conjugacy of involutions by complex automorphisms.

Root-system conventions: a reduced crystallographic root system is reduced (the only integral multiples of a root that are roots are ±α) and lives in a real inner product space; the empty root system has zero ambient space and counts as irreducible under the local convention, so it is a separate rank-zero case in the classification.

Haar-measure convention: on a compact Lie group the normalized Haar measure is the unique regular Borel probability measure invariant under left translations, right translations and inversion (bi-invariance is automatic, not an extra hypothesis).

Weyl Jacobian convention: J(t) = ∏_{α∈Φ+}|1 − α(t)^{−1}|^2 with the quotient measure on G/T fixed by the coset Fubini identity using the right-translation convention, so that the exponent −1 is the one matching the integration formula.

Choice-principle convention: each item states its own hypothesis explicitly; the complex Lie-theoretic, compact-group and real-form pages and their examples assume the Axiom of Choice, while the moment-map page and several examples assume only the Axiom of Countable Choice (weaker, hence supplied by AC where AC is assumed).

load_bearing.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let g be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra, h a Cartan subalgebra, and Φ its root set. Then Φ is finite and g = h ⊕ ⨁_{α∈Φ} g_α is a direct sum of h with the nonzero root spaces.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a Cartan subalgebra h of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra g with root set Φ and Cartan integers ⟨β,α^∨⟩ = β(h_α): (i) Φ is finite and g = h ⊕ ⨁_{α∈Φ} g_α with dim g_α = 1; (ii) Φ spans h*; (iii) Φ is reduced and closed under negation; (iv) s_α(β) ∈ Φ; (v) ⟨β,α^∨⟩ ∈ ℤ. Thus Φ satisfies the axioms of a reduced crystallographic root system with coroots α^∨ = h_α; only the listed properties are asserted here.

Let Φ be an irreducible reduced crystallographic root system. If Φ is empty its ambient space is zero and it is irreducible under the local convention; otherwise Φ is isomorphic, as a root system, to exactly one of A_n (n ≥ 1), B_n (n ≥ 2), C_n (n ≥ 3), D_n (n ≥ 4), E_6, E_7, E_8, F_4, G_2, with the low-rank identifications B_1 = C_1 = A_1, B_2 = C_2, D_2 = A_1 ⊔ A_1 and D_3 = A_3.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-type Cartan matrix A of size r with Serre Lie algebra g(A): g(A) is finite-dimensional and semisimple, has a Cartan subalgebra h spanned by the images of the h_i, has root system Φ(A) with Cartan matrix A, and has the triangular decomposition g(A) = n_− ⊕ h ⊕ n_+; if r > 0 and A is irreducible then g(A) is simple. Conversely, if g is a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with base Δ and root sl_2 triples (e_i,f_i,h_i), then those triples generate g and satisfy exactly the Serre relations, so g ≅ g(A).

Let sl_2 have basis (e,f,h) and let V be a finite-dimensional module. (i) V is a direct sum of irreducible submodules. (ii) If V ≠ 0 is irreducible, there is an integer m ≥ 0 with dim V = m+1 and h diagonalisable with eigenvalues m, m−2, …, −m, each on a one-dimensional subspace. (iii) For arbitrary finite-dimensional V ≠ 0, h acts diagonalisably with integer eigenvalues.

For a Cartan subalgebra h of a complex semisimple g, α ∈ Φ and β ∈ Φ ∪ {0}, the set {k ∈ ℤ : g_{β+kα} ≠ 0} is a nonempty interval of consecutive integers {−p, …, q} with p, q ≥ 0 and p − q = β(h_α) ∈ ℤ.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra has a Cartan subalgebra; indeed every maximal toral subalgebra of such an algebra is a Cartan subalgebra.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two Cartan subalgebras of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra are carried to one another by an inner automorphism in the connected adjoint group; in particular all Cartan subalgebras have the same dimension.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For g complex semisimple with Cartan h and root set Φ, put E = span_R Φ and h_R = span_R{h_α : α ∈ Φ}. Then every λ ∈ E is real valued on h_R with restriction a linear isomorphism E → Hom_R(h_R, R); h_R is a real form of h and the Killing form restricted to h_R is positive definite; and (λ,μ) := B(H_λ,H_μ) makes Φ a reduced crystallographic Euclidean root system in E.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra g with Cartan subalgebra h and a fixed positive system, the maps V ↦ λ(V) and λ ↦ L(λ) are mutually inverse bijections between isomorphism classes of finite-dimensional irreducible representations of g and dominant integral weights.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every compact Lie group has a unique regular Borel probability measure invariant under left and right translations and inversion.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Any two maximal tori of a compact connected Lie group are conjugate.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let G be a compact connected Lie group with maximal torus T. Then the faithful action of W(G,T) on the semisimple part of t identifies it with the Weyl group generated by the root reflections: for every root α the associated compact root SU(2) supplies a cocharacter α^∨ : S^1 → T with ⟨α,α^∨⟩ = 2, and conjugation by its standard normalizer element acts on t by the reflection s_α; the resulting reflections generate W(G,T).

Assume the Axiom of Choice. For a compact Lie group G with normalized Haar measure, the normalized matrix coefficients sqrt(d_π) π_ij, over a set of representatives of the irreducible unitary finite-dimensional representations and orthonormal bases of each, form an orthonormal Hilbert basis of L^2(G); moreover the π-isotypic summand of the left regular representation occurs with multiplicity dim π.
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Every finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra g has a compact real form k_0, that is, a real form whose Killing form B|_{k_0 × k_0} is negative definite.

Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let g be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra. Sending a real form to its Vogan diagram induces a bijection between isomorphism classes of real forms of g and equivalence classes of abstract Vogan diagrams over its root system, with the conventions of the Vogan-diagram definition (an involution of a based Dynkin diagram, a painted subset of its fixed vertices, and equivalence generated by diagram isomorphisms and the prescribed reflections at painted vertices).

Assume AC_ω. For a smooth action on a symplectic manifold with fundamental fields ξ_M, components μ^ξ(p) := ⟨μ(p),ξ⟩; μ is an infinitesimal moment map when dμ^ξ = −ι_{ξ_M}ω for every ξ, an equivariant moment map when in addition μ(g·p) = g·μ(p) for the coadjoint action, and a Hamiltonian action is a symplectic action admitting an equivariant moment map.

Assume AC_ω. Let (M,ω,G,μ) be a Hamiltonian G-space, α a regular value of μ, and suppose the coadjoint stabilizer G_α acts freely and properly on μ^{-1}(α). Then M_α := μ^{-1}(α)/G_α is a smooth manifold and there is a unique symplectic form ω_α on M_α with π^*ω_α = ι^*ω.

published_dependencies.used_for: The Axiom of Choice assumed in the statement of essentially every item of this group (Jordan decomposition, Cartan theory, root systems, highest weight theory, compact Lie groups, real forms); verified it is the standard choice-function statement.
The weaker AC_ω assumed by the moment-map page items and several examples; AC_ω is implied by the AC assumed on the other pages.

Supplies the additive Jordan–Chevalley decomposition (unique commuting semisimple + nilpotent parts, polynomial in T) invoked by the batch-11 abstract Jordan decomposition items. Its statement assumes AC, but its deps field omits def-axiom-of-choice (already recorded as a published AC-metadata gap at step 5a; not repaired here since published content is out of this dispatch's write scope).
Der(g) = ad(g) for finite-dimensional semisimple g in characteristic zero, used in the conjugacy of compact real forms and the existence/conjugacy of Cartan involutions.
Z(g) = 0 and [g,g] = g, used where inner derivations/automorphisms must be unique or where the derived algebra must be all of g.
Invariance of trace forms (and hence of the Killing form), used in the root-space orthogonality theory and the real-forms arguments.
Semisimplicity ⟺ nondegenerate Killing form, used throughout the classical examples and the real-form existence theorems.
Normalizations K_{sl_n}(X,Y) = 2n tr(XY), K_{so_n} = (n−2) tr(XY), K_{sp_{2n}} = 2(n+1) tr(XY), used by the highest-weight and real-form examples for sl_n.
K(h,h) = 8 and K(e,f) = 4 for sl_2, used by the sl_2 compact/split real-form examples and the Killing-signature counterexample.
A commuting family of diagonalisable endomorphisms is simultaneously diagonalisable, used in conjugacy of maximal tori, restricted-root decompositions and θ-stable Cartan arguments.
Generalised eigenspace (primary) decomposition of an endomorphism, used by the generalized weight space decomposition for a nilpotent subalgebra.
Existence of regular elements (avoiding finitely many root hyperplanes), used for Cartan subalgebras, positive restricted roots and Vogan/Satake positive systems.
H^2(g,M) = 0 for g semisimple, used to remove the infinitesimal equivariance obstruction for semisimple Hamiltonian actions.
Complete reducibility of finite-dimensional modules over a semisimple Lie algebra, used in the highest-weight decomposition corollary and in the Serre converse argument.
Existence and uniqueness of X_H with ι_{X_H}ω = dH, used to turn moment-map components into Hamiltonian vector fields and to descend flows.
su(2) ≅ so(3) with non-isomorphic connected groups, used by the coadjoint-orbit and nonfree-level moment-map examples.
Nonzero period obstructs exactness of a closed form, used by the counterexample that an irrational flow on the symplectic torus is not Hamiltonian.
Common eigenvector for solvable Lie algebras, used in the Cartan subalgebra existence/nilpotent-decomposition theory.
Nilpotency criterion via ad-nilpotent elements, used in the Cartan subalgebra and generalized weight space arguments.
Equivalences characterising trees, used by the lemma that finite irreducible Dynkin diagrams are trees with controlled branching.
Inner-product conventions (linear in the first argument, conjugate-linear in the second), used where Euclidean root systems and compact-group inner products are set up.
PBW basis of the enveloping algebra, used by the survival lemma for the dominant cyclic module, Verma-module and symmetric/exterior-power examples, and weight arguments.
The surjective two-sheeted covering SU(2) → SO(3) with kernel {±I}, used by the counterexample that the full weight lattice does not integrate to every central quotient.

concerns.concern: Step 3.1 opens 'Combining steps 1.1-3.1 gives the assertions', but 3.1 is the step itself; the intended range is 1.1–2.1, as the bracketed citations [step 1.1, step 1.2, step 2.1] show. A self-referential range with a nonexistent endpoint; no mathematical content is affected.

Statement item 4 reads '...stable under conjugation averaging H ↦ ∫_G H(x^{-1}·x) dx and under inversion when the corresponding symmetries preserve the subspace'. The integral is written with the integration variable both as x and as the exponentiated argument, and the second clause ('when the corresponding symmetries preserve the subspace') is conditional and vague: as written it asserts stability under inversion only for subspaces already preserved by inversion, which makes the clause nearly automatic. The intended content (that conjugation-averaging is available on central kernels and that inversion-stable subspaces are inherited when the subspace is) needs a precise statement.

Residual recorded by the 5a adjudication (defect row phase-2-remaining-27-a-5a-16, disposition 'narrowed', nonfatal, open): step 5.1's argument that lambda ∈ Q_+ with lambda ≠ 0 and more than one positive coefficient has a simple-root reflection image of smaller height (using c = lambda(h_i) an integer, and that some other coefficient stays positive) is compressed, and the statement of dimension count dim g(A) = r + |Φ(A)| rests on it. The earlier residual about the invariant form no longer applies to the current bytes (steps 4.1 and 5.1 no longer cite an invariant form), but this compressed step should be adjudicated on the current text.

seams_checked.note: Opened lem-l-two-with-the-integral-pairing-is-a-hilbert-space (AC_ω; L^2 of any measure space with ⟨f,g⟩ = ∫ f ḡ is a complex Hilbert space with the quotient norm), thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties ((TS)* = S*T*, T** = T, ‖T*T‖ = ‖T‖^2), thm-l-two-kernels-give-hilbert-schmidt-operators (sigma-finite spaces, k ∈ L^2 of the completed product, T_k Hilbert–Schmidt with ‖T_k‖_HS = ‖k‖_2) and thm-hilbert-schmidt-operators-are-compact. The citing texts are faithful: def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations-on-l-two-of-a-compact-lie-group cites the L^2 Hilbert-space lemma for G compact (finite measure, so sigma-finiteness holds) under the stronger AC; lem-continuous-convolution-operators-are-hilbert-schmidt-and-compact cites the kernel theorem in the form 'If k ∈ L^2(G×G) is a kernel class, the associated operator T on L^2(G) is Hilbert–Schmidt with ‖T‖_HS = ‖k‖_2' plus compactness, matching the cited statement exactly; lem-compact-convolution-operators-decompose-into-finite-dimensional-invariant-subspaces cites only clauses (TS)* = S*T*, T** = T, ‖T*T‖ = ‖T‖^2 of the adjoint theorem, with hypotheses no stronger than the cited ones (the Countable Choice hypotheses of the suppliers are weaker than the citing items' AC).

Opened thm-hilbert-space-fourier-expansion (AC_ω; for a complete orthonormal family (e_i)_{i∈I} in a real or complex Hilbert space, x = Σ_i ⟨x,e_i⟩e_i as the norm limit of the finite-subset net, with coefficient uniqueness and unconditional enumeration) and thm-fourier-basis-and-parseval-on-the-n-torus. The citing text of thm-peter-weyl-for-compact-lie-groups states '[L5] A complete orthonormal family gives the norm-convergent finite-subset Fourier expansion', which states the cited proposition itself (its completeness hypothesis is established in step 3.1 of that proof), not a summary of its use. ex-fourier-series-on-a-torus-as-peter-weyl cites the torus theorem for the Fourier basis/Parseval statement and explicitly treats the rank-zero case r = 0 directly because the cited theorem assumes n ≥ 1, so no hypothesis is dropped in either direction.

Opened thm-spectral-theorem-for-compact-self-adjoint-operators (AC_ω; nonzero eigenvalues real with finite-dimensional eigenspaces, no accumulation except at 0, and the closed span M of the eigenspaces satisfies M = (ker T)^⊥ = closure(ran T)). The citing item lem-compact-convolution-operators-decompose-into-finite-dimensional-invariant-subspaces states this as 'for a compact self-adjoint operator the set of nonzero eigenvalues consists of real numbers with finite-dimensional eigenspaces and the closed span of the eigenspaces is the orthogonal complement of the kernel, equal to the closure of the range' — domain, quantifiers and both equalities preserved, and the citing item's AC supplies the supplier's Countable Choice. The same item also cites thm-hilbert-adjoint-properties from the sibling page, checked above.
